overview: Stepped multi-site mixed methods evaluation over 18 months in four hospitals, restricted to adult ward rapid response calls: a three-month baseline in all hospitals, then monthly in-situ simulation with structured debriefing introduced one hospital every three months in a random order, with a quantitative strand on real adult ward calls and a qualitative strand on experience, integrated by joint displays.
exposure: Monthly unannounced in-situ simulation on a general ward with the on-duty rapid response team, followed by a 20-minute structured debrief by trained faculty; latent safety threats logged in the hospital safety tracking system.
procedures: Adult ward call data (activation time, first critical intervention time, disposition) are abstracted from the rapid response call record by trained abstractors blind to the programme phase where possible; paediatric and obstetric calls are excluded because those units have separate teams. Simulations follow a safety protocol: advance notice to the ward manager, signage, a stop word, and immediate cancellation if a real call occurs. The qualitative strand interviews adult rapid response team members, ward nurses and families and observes debriefs in each hospital after introduction.

outcomes.name: Time from call to first critical intervention
outcomes.measure: Minutes from call activation to the first of a defined list of critical interventions, from the call record
outcomes.why: The real-call outcome most responsive to team training (claim c1).

outcomes.name: Unplanned intensive care admission within 12 hours of a call
outcomes.measure: Admission to intensive care within 12 hours not planned before the call
outcomes.why: Patient outcome, expected to move little.

outcomes.name: Death within 24 hours of a call
outcomes.measure: Death within 24 hours, excluding patients with a prior comfort-care order
outcomes.why: Safety check; too rare for inference.

outcomes.name: Simulations delivered and latent safety threats resolved
outcomes.measure: Proportion of planned monthly simulations delivered; threats resolved within 30 days

outcomes.name: Experiences of teams, ward nurses and families
outcomes.measure: Themes from interviews and debrief observation
outcomes.why: Explains how and why real-call performance changes or not.

feasibility: Eight faculty hours a month per hospital cover one simulation and debrief on an adult ward; abstraction of about 2,310 adult ward calls a year and the interviews are funded from the 48,000 grant.
biasMitigation: Abstractors blind to phase where possible

biasFlags.label: Secular trends across 18 months
biasFlags.note: Handled by calendar-time adjustment in the stepped analysis.

biasFlags.label: Few clusters
biasFlags.note: Four hospitals give few degrees of freedom; small-sample corrections.

biasFlags.label: Contamination between hospitals
biasFlags.note: Staff who work at two hospitals are recorded.

flags: One quantitative primary outcome; the qualitative strand is reported as its own aim
parsimony.simplestPath: One primary real-call outcome, four hospitals introduced in random order, interviews after introduction.

theoreticalFramework: Kirkpatrick levels to place outcomes (behaviour and results over reaction), and a convergent joint display for integration; no other framework.
summary: Protocol reconciled with the investigator's restriction to adult ward calls; population text kept as the investigator wrote it.
